briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. Welcome to the climate briefing for October 16, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Climate Crisis: Domestic and International Warnings and Impacts
sections.content: Today, severe impacts and warnings due to climate change resonated both domestically and internationally. In South Korea, a 'Bukang-i' phenomenon, involving shark sightings in Busan, has raised concerns as a sign of climate change [1]. An analysis also indicated that the need for water level control at Unmun Dam and a decrease in large-scale hydropower generation are attributable to climate change [2]. Internationally, climate change is exacerbating the humanitarian situation in Sudan [46], and is having widespread effects such as increased mortality costs [48], growing difficulties in animal control operations [49], and rising crop costs in Mexico [53]. Furthermore, analyses and research findings were released, suggesting that global warming had a greater impact than El Niño in intensifying Hurricanes Isaias and Polo [52, 63]. El Niño, climate change, and human activities were identified as causes for the surge in Amazon fires [57]. Globally, direct damages from climate change are spreading, including the declaration of severe drought in six regions of the UK due to reservoir depletion [68], leading to instances of insurance companies withdrawing from certain markets [54].

sections.title: 🌱 Efforts Towards a Carbon-Neutral Society: Domestic and International Initiatives
sections.content: Amidst this crisis, diverse efforts to transition towards a carbon-neutral society are actively continuing both domestically and internationally. In South Korea, blueberry farming methods in the Gimhae region are changing in response to climate change, with farmer education underway [3]. In Pohang, rice variety evaluations are being conducted to find 'customized rice' that can overcome the climate crisis [5]. Carbon-neutral ideas from future generations are being applied in corporate settings [4], and Dongdaemun-gu is encouraging citizen participation by operating mobile carbon-neutral experience booths for apartment complexes [12, 15, 21]. Seventeen carbon neutrality support centers nationwide gathered in Daegu to build a cooperation network and enhance the effectiveness of regional greenhouse gas reduction [13, 29]. Goyang City is pursuing 105 projects with the goal of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 36% by 2030 [30]. Internationally, Hyundai Engineering has achieved results in its climate change response support project in Vietnam [6], and major U.S. cities have shown proactive efforts in preparing for climate change [60]. Additionally, the climate change film 'Weather under Fire' is gaining attention, contributing to raising public awareness [44].

sections.title: 🌱 Renewable Energy Expansion and Technological Innovation
sections.content: In the renewable energy sector, efforts in technological innovation and infrastructure expansion are continuing. Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO) is collaborating with the Korea Meteorological Administration to advance AI-based renewable energy generation forecasting technology [32, 35], which is a significant step towards stable grid integration of renewable energy. Domestically, Kim Jun-dong, CEO of Korea Southern Power (KOSPO), mentioned the Dadaepo offshore wind power project as a step towards achieving carbon neutrality in Busan [11], and SK Oceanplant participated in a Taiwan renewable energy exhibition to showcase its offshore wind power technology [34]. Internationally, large-scale renewable energy projects are underway, including the completion of the Kohawai Park Solar Farm in New Zealand [36], the commencement of commercial operation for the Villameca 200MWp solar power plant in Spain [40], and the groundbreaking of the Holtzheim wind farm in Munich [38]. Grid modernization and renewable energy integration are expected to drive growth in related markets such as transformer insulation pressboard [37], high-voltage electric capacitors [39], and surge suppressors [41]. Furthermore, the importance of renewable energy is gaining greater social recognition, with the establishment of the 'first official commemorative day' embodying the aspirations of those in the renewable energy sector [33].

sections.title: 🌍 Climate Policy, Legal Responsibility, and the Reality and Challenges of International Cooperation
sections.content: The current state of climate change response policies, legal responsibilities, and international cooperation presents a mixed picture. During a domestic parliamentary audit, it was pointed out that 6,670 charging stations, which cost 1.7 trillion won, are currently inoperative, and there is a lack of participating entities for the carbon neutrality points system [25]. There was also an exclusive report stating that the 'Green Certification System' is failing to accurately assess actual carbon reduction effects [43]. Internationally, discussions on legal responsibility are expanding, with 17 organizations in Montana filing a lawsuit demanding that the Public Service Commission be mandated to consider climate change [45, 47], and a county in Pennsylvania proceeding with a climate change tort lawsuit at the appellate level [50]. Meanwhile, at the COP17 meeting in Armenia, the first global review of progress towards the UN's 2030 nature targets is expected [69]. However, developed countries' nature finance targets were found to be 'significantly falling short' [70], indicating financial challenges for international cooperation. Turkmenistan is seeking international solidarity by proposing a platform for addressing climate change and drought [66].

briefing.closing: As we have seen in today's briefing, the warnings of the climate crisis are becoming increasingly clear, yet diverse domestic and international efforts to overcome it are also actively underway. However, challenges such as policy effectiveness and international financial support still remain, requiring continuous attention and effort. This concludes today's climate briefing.
